scope.evidence_basis: Actual original-source comparison and local derivation reread: Checked K(0)=0, [cv]=c[v], and ||K(x)||<=C||x||^alpha by scaling the unit ball. Compactness of gauge-bounded sets follows from compact images of bounded input sets. With alpha>=1 and p>=1, Holder gives ||u||L1<=T^(1-1/(alpha p))G^(1/alpha), with factor T at infinity. Strong measurability of u is separately assumed, not inferred from injectivity. The W11 output bound supplies every fixed r>1; finite-p or supremum translations follow in E2. The reduction requires derivatives in E2. A weaker-space derivative cannot be renamed, and noninjective maps do not admit this inverse gauge. Compared the three route interfaces. Linear averaging uses a vector space; nonlinear truncation uses a compact hull; the cone route combines truncation in A1 and a two-point upgrade to A0. A common criterion does not prove equivalence of hypotheses.
